Optional spatial and phenotype analyses

SpPrAn 0.3.1 adds three optional analyses to the unsupervised/full workflow. They complement phenotype discovery rather than replacing it.

Protein-marker intensity spatial plots

The intensity_spatial_plot option creates a spatial map for each sample and protein marker.

Each segmented cell remains at its tissue coordinate and is colored by the continuous intensity stored in the AnnData matrix.

Configuration example:

intensity_spatial_plot:
  dpi: 150
  scatter_point_size: 50

Biological interpretation

These maps answer where high or low measured protein intensity occurs in the tissue.

They are conceptually similar to displaying gene expression on a UMAP, except that the x/y positions are true tissue coordinates rather than embedding coordinates.

Caution

The current implementation scales each sample/protein marker plot independently from its observed minimum and maximum intensity. Colors should therefore be interpreted within a panel and should not be treated as a quantitatively harmonized scale across samples.

Fixed-radius neighborhood analysis

The nhood_analysis option constructs spatial neighborhoods directly from cell coordinates.

Example:

nhood_analysis:
  nhood_radius_size: 50
  pixel_conversion_rate: 1
  max_distance_coocurrence: 200
  dpi: 150

The radius supplied to Squidpy is:

neighborhood_radius_size / pixel_conversion_rate

The analysis does not use PCA or expression-space nearest neighbors.

Neighborhood enrichment

Neighborhood enrichment compares the observed adjacency of major cell populations with a permutation-based expectation.

Positive z-scores indicate population pairs found near each other more often than expected; negative values indicate depletion/avoidance.

SpPrAn exports both the complete heatmap and population-highlighted views.

Interaction matrix

The interaction matrix summarizes direct neighborhood relationships among major cell populations using the fixed-radius spatial graph.

SpPrAn exports a complete matrix plus highlighted views for individual populations.

Co-occurrence analysis

Co-occurrence analysis describes how the spatial association of populations changes with distance.

max_distance_coocurrence controls the largest distance displayed on the co-occurrence figure. It changes the displayed x-axis range rather than the radius used to construct the neighborhood graph.

Important

Neighborhood association is not equivalent to causal cell-cell communication. Spatial proximity may support a biological hypothesis, but mechanism requires additional evidence.

Advanced phenotype classification

Set:

advanced_cell_classification: true

to further characterize discovered phenotypes using protein intensity.

The initial unsupervised phenotype remains defined by protein marker positivity. Advanced classification then describes the intensity of positive protein markers.

For each sample and protein marker:

  • protein-marker-negative cells are labeled Absent;

  • positive cells below the 25th percentile are Low;

  • positive cells from the 25th through 75th percentile are Medium; and

  • positive cells above the 75th percentile are High.

Thresholds are calculated independently in each sample.

Outputs

Advanced classification generates:

Protein marker intensity summary.csv

Low/medium/high counts and proportions for each positive protein marker within each discovered phenotype.

Intensity profiles analysis.csv

Observed combinations of protein-marker-intensity states within each phenotype and their relative frequencies.

Phenotype intensity summary.csv

Phenotype-level overview including the number of positive protein markers, number of observed intensity profiles, and frequency of the most common profile.

The intensity classes and threshold metadata are also stored in AnnData when AnnData saving is enabled.

Biological interpretation

The low/medium/high categories are sample-relative intensity descriptors. They should not be interpreted as universal expression thresholds across patients or experiments without additional normalization/harmonization.

This distinction is important in tumor-microenvironment analyses: a cell can belong to the same positivity-defined phenotype in two tumors while exhibiting different relative protein-expression strengths.
